chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام: A woman sits by the head of a sick person while she is menstruating, when he is at the point of death. He said: “There is no problem in her nursing him; but when they fear for him and that draws near, then she should be moved away from him and from his proximity, for indeed the angels are harmed by that.”

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةَ: the angels present in relation to the dying person
key_terms.تُمَرِّضَهُ: to nurse him or care for him during illness
key_terms.فِي حَدِّ الْمَوْتِ: at the point or verge of death
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection or harm in doing so

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman sit near or nurse a person who is at the point of death?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a menstruating woman attending a dying sick person. It permits her to nurse him, but when death becomes imminent she should be kept away from his immediate proximity, because the angels are harmed by that.
